propositions: Canonical rebar bridge status and hidden rebar bridge-status must parse identically and expose the same core, options, output formats, and exit codes without removing old vocabulary.

A single process-finalizer writer records authoritative minimal JSON to refs/reconciler/last-pass before releasing refs/reconciler/lock, with observed-OID CAS bounded to three attempts, 100ms and 200ms retry delays, and loud failure on exhausted contention or push error.

Status verdict precedence is PAUSED > RUNNING > FOREIGN > FAILED > STALE > HEALTHY, with NEVER_RUN when no record and no live lock; status is a fast read-only snapshot that never mutates or steals locks.
Explicit REBAR_ENV_ID wins; otherwise writer and status derive stable local:<repo-env-id> from checkout .env-id, treating missing or unreadable .env-id as a hard configuration error.

Canary moves from GitHub Actions heartbeat polling to durable git state by fetching refs/reconciler/*, targeting reconciler, detecting crash via two read-only live-fence snapshots across the lock-held lease, and defaulting to status source after one producer write.

One rolling .bridge_state/last-pass.json supplies rich detail matched by pass and environment ids; ADR 0094 documents the design, extends ADR 0031 prior art, and follows the current numbering convention.
